reviews.title: Great case, and easy to setup.
reviews.comment: The price of this case is unbeatable, especially when you consider the popular fish tank aesthetic and the inclusion of multiple ARGB fans along with a hub. I had no issues fitting an ATX motherboard inside—it’s spacious and well-designed. Airflow is excellent, and I mounted a 280mm AIO at the top without any problems. Once the fans were calibrated through the BIOS, the case's performance really stood out. For anyone looking for a visually appealing case with great cooling potential, this is a solid choice.
reviews.author: alex

reviews.title: Great value in a case, really need a bit more room at the bottom of the case
reviews.comment:
Why did I pick this?  My interest was piqued by these new dual chamber cases and I have never built inside one.  I realize they are wider than a traditional case but I was willing to go in this direction.  I also wanted updated USB front panel connecters.  NZXT H6 was a close second because I have built inside at least 6 NZXT H210 cases and they are quality cases.  The C5 included a fan controller and 7 ARGB fans and that swayed me in that direction.
Overall impression is good.  If it just had another 25-35mm of space past the edge of the bottom of the motherboard for cable management that would have been perfect.  The bottom edge of the ATX motherboard sits next to the fans.  I had to take out a fan to get the GPU cables in this area.  You can see the limited room in one of the attached pictures.  Still have lots of spaghetti in the back.  Overall a very sweet case.

reviews.author: Anthony

reviews.title: Great case for high-end builds, with solid airflow and style
reviews.comment:
Running the Antec C5 ARGB White with my ASRock B650 Steel Legend motherboard, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, and NVIDIA 4070 Ti Super. The case fits the Arctic Liquid Freezer 3 360mm AIO cooler perfectly—no clearance issues at all, which is a huge relief.
The seven 120mm ARGB fans are great—plenty of airflow and the lighting adds a nice visual punch without being over the top. Cable management is pretty easy too, with lots of routing holes and tie points to keep everything neat inside.
Build quality feels solid for the price, and the tempered glass side panel really shows off the components nicely. The white finish looks sleek, though it does attract fingerprints more than I expected—so be ready to clean it now and then.
One minor gripe: the front panel filter is a bit flimsy and could be more secure, which sometimes makes it a bit fiddly when removing or replacing it. Not a dealbreaker, but something to keep in mind.
All in all, this case hits a sweet spot between airflow, aesthetics, and compatibility for a high-performance Ryzen 7000-series setup like mine. Definitely recommend if you want a stylish case that doesn’t compromise on cooling or space
